key_insight: DexCompose shows that dexterous hand policies do not need to be learned from scratch for every task. By composing pretrained skills in a role-aware way, a single hand can reuse existing behaviors while adding new ones with less interference.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the difficulty of combining multiple dexterous manipulation skills on one hand. New tasks often conflict with existing ones because the same fingers and contact modes must satisfy competing objectives, leading to destructive interference.
method: Introduces DexCompose, a role-aware residual composition framework for reusing pretrained dexterous policies.
Separates manipulation roles so the system can preserve the original skill while selectively adding residual control for the new task.
Designed to reduce overlap-induced conflict between tasks that share fingers, contacts, or motion patterns.
impact: This matters because it can make dexterous manipulation more scalable and data-efficient, especially when practitioners want to build multi-task systems without training a new policy for every skill. It also offers a practical path toward reusable robot hand capabilities in real-world settings.
visual_elements: Before/after diagram showing a single policy vs. composed multi-task policy
Hand illustration with color-coded finger roles and contact points
Flowchart of pretrained skill + residual adapter = composed behavior
Conflict visualization showing overlapping task demands and how DexCompose reduces interference
paper_title: DexCompose: Reusing Dexterous Policies for Multi-Task Manipulation with a Single Hand
paper_authors: Dihong Huang, Zhenyu Wei, Zhuxiu Xu, Yunchao Yao, Sikai Li
